results.content:
## What is the free-threaded build of Python 3.13?

The free-threaded build of Python 3.13 is CPython compiled with the Global Interpreter Lock disabled. The standard CPython build uses the GIL to prevent multiple native threads from executing Python bytecode simultaneously; the free-threaded build removes that interpreter-level restriction so genuinely parallel threads can run Python code on multiple CPU cores.

Drivers · Free Tool

### Crashes, No Sound, or Screen Glitches? [...] Python 3.13 free threading trades some single-threaded efficiency for the possibility of parallel Python execution. According to the Python 3.13 free-threading HOWTO, the free-threaded build has approximately 40% overhead on the pyperformance suite compared with the default GIL-enabled build.  Python 3.13’s free-threaded build carries approximately 40% overhead on the official pyperformance suite compared with the default build, so it is not a universal speed upgrade.
 Native extensions can lack compatible wheels or automatically re-enable the GIL when imported.
 Free threading permits parallel execution but does not make shared mutable state, iterators, or frame inspection automatically safe.
